instructions: Make the sauce first. In a small saucepan, stir together 1 1/2 cups of water, the dashi granules, the soy sauce, the mirin and the sugar. Bring it to a boil, then simmer for 2 minutes until the sugar dissolves. Take it off the heat.

Peel the daikon, grate it on the small holes of a box grater, and squeeze out a little of the liquid. That should be about 1/2 cup. Put 2 tbsp in each of 4 small bowls and pour in about 1/3 cup of the warm sauce.

Slice the sweet potatoes into thin rounds, about 1/8 inch. Slice the mushrooms lengthwise, cut the pepper into strips, and trim the green beans. Pat everything dry with paper towels. Wet vegetables make the batter slide off.

Pour the oil into a Dutch oven or heavy pot until it is about 1 1/2 inches deep, and heat it over medium-high to 340°F. If you have no thermometer, drop in a pea-sized bit of batter once it's made. It should sink a little, then float up and sizzle.
Set a wire rack over a baking sheet next to the stove.

Just before frying, whisk the eggs and 1 2/3 cups of iced water in a large bowl. Add the flour all at once and stir with chopsticks or a fork for 15 seconds. Leave the lumps. Set the bowl in a larger bowl of ice.

Dip a few sweet potato slices in the batter, let the extra drip off for 2 seconds, and lower them into the oil. Stand back a little. They'll spatter. Fry in small batches for 2 minutes, until pale gold, and transfer them to the rack.
Fry the mushrooms, pepper strips and green beans the same way, 1 to 2 minutes a batch. Skim the crumbs out of the oil between batches.
Serve the tempura hot with the bowls of dipping sauce and grated daikon.
method_notes: Lead is Just One Cookbook's vegetable tempura (4.68 from 93): an egg, iced water and flour batter mixed for 15 seconds and left lumpy, a tentsuyu of dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar, and grated daikon in the sauce. Kikkoman's version uses a smaller batter with baking powder and fries at 338°F. The lead's sweet potato, kabocha, lotus root, eggplant and shiso are swapped for sweet potato, king oyster mushroom, bell pepper and green beans from the Kikkoman list, and the sweet potato is cut thinner so it fries in 2 minutes. The dashi is a vegetarian kombu dashi, since ordinary dashi is made with bonito. Doubled for 4, this is not honestly a 30 minute dinner because the frying goes in batches.
